name: Astera Labs
thesis: Astera Labs sells PCIe, CXL and Ethernet connectivity chips for AI racks; Q2 revenue was $392M (+105% y/y). It closed Oct 23 at $257.16, 33% below the Oct 7 close of $382.25, and was $259.19 (+0.8%) early Monday Oct 26. No company news since Oct 12.
risks: A beta near 3.8 means 10% days on sector headlines alone; Meta's Q3 filing showed $810B of future lease and contract commitments, which fed worries about debt-funded AI build-outs.
catalyst: Alphabet and Microsoft capex comments Oct 28-29 US (Oct 29-30 AEDT); Q3 results Nov 3 after US close, call 4:30pm ET (08:30 AEDT Wed Nov 4).

name: Broadcom
thesis: Broadcom supplies custom AI accelerators (Google, Meta, OpenAI) plus Ethernet networking and VMware. Meta launched a raise of up to $95B in stock on Oct 26 to fund AI build-outs, and Broadcom, Nvidia and AMD indicated (non-binding) interest in buying up to $5B of it. AVGO was $326.65 (+1.5%) early Monday.
risks: Broadcom now finances customers twice over (OpenAI chip purchases, possibly Meta equity), so it is exposed if AI buyers cannot fund capex; Meta's Q3 free cash flow was -$2.1B.
catalyst: Alphabet and Microsoft capex comments Oct 28-29 US (Oct 29-30 AEDT); Q4 FY26 results around Dec 10 (not yet confirmed).

name: Celestica
thesis: Celestica builds 800G/1.6T networking switches, servers and storage for hyperscalers; it guided Q3 to $5.25-5.55B revenue and $2.88-3.08 EPS and 2026 to $20.5B. It closed Oct 23 at $260.01 (-14.6% since Oct 21) and was $262.19 (+0.8%) early Monday ahead of tonight's report. Results not out at time of writing.
risks: Single-digit hardware margins and a few hyperscaler customers; 2027 targets at the investor day will be judged against fears of a capex digestion year. CEO and CFO sold shares in the past three months.
catalyst: Q3 results Mon Oct 26 after US close (about 07:15 AEDT Tue Oct 27); call and Investor Day Tue Oct 27, 8:00am ET (23:00 AEDT Tue Oct 27).

name: Credo Technology
thesis: Credo sells active electrical cables (AECs), optical DSPs and retimers; fiscal Q1 2027 revenue was $479M (+115% y/y). It fell 19.2% over Oct 22-23 to $147.29 after MaxLinear said on its Oct 22 call it will target 20-30% of 1.6T AECs within a couple of years (it puts Credo's share at 93-99%), and third-party research flagged slower 1.6T rollouts. Conviction cut to low until fiscal Q2 shows the 1.6T ramp.
risks: A credible second source in AECs would hit pricing from fiscal 2028; a few hyperscalers drive most revenue, and the CEO and CTO have been selling under 10b5-1 plans.
catalyst: Fiscal Q2 2027 quarter ends about Oct 31; results early December (date not announced).

name: SK hynix ADR
thesis: SK hynix is the leading HBM supplier to Nvidia and the number-two DRAM maker. Dong-A Ilbo reported Oct 26 it is weighing a special dividend of about KRW 16T ($12B) from its Kioxia gains, possibly announced with Q3 on Wednesday; the company says a shareholder-return plan comes then but no dividend is decided. Seoul shares closed Oct 26 at KRW 1.28M (-0.16%) as the KOSPI fell 1.46%; the ADR was $141.47 (+3.3%) early Monday.
risks: CXMT closing the density gap would pressure DRAM prices from 2027; foreigners sold KRW 696B of Korean stocks on Oct 26, and a smaller-than-reported payout would disappoint after the run-up.
catalyst: Q3 results, call and shareholder-return plan Wed Oct 28, 9:00am KST (11:00 AEDT Wed Oct 28); Samsung full Q3 results Thu Oct 29 (12:00 AEDT).

name: Bloom Energy
thesis: Bloom makes solid-oxide fuel cells for onsite data-centre power. Q3 revenue was a record $1.236B (+138% y/y), product revenue +179%, adjusted EPS $0.94 vs $0.69 expected, and 2026 guidance was raised a third time to $4.4-4.6B (from $3.9-4.2B). The stock fell 19% over Oct 22-23 to $193.30 on Q3 free cash flow of -$181M and the AI selloff, so forward P/E is about 40x vs 78x on Sep 30. Upgraded to accumulate.
risks: Capex of $153M (from $12M) to double capacity turned Q3 cash flow negative; delivery depends on Oracle and Brookfield sites arriving on time; Jefferies cut its target to $242 from $289 after the print.
catalyst: Oracle Jupiter permit Nov 23; 2027 guidance and backlog figure with Q4 results (February).

name: GE Vernova
thesis: GE Vernova builds gas turbines, grid equipment and wind for the power build-out; Q2 orders rose 88% y/y and backlog is $176B. It closed Oct 23 at $815.00, about 31% below the June 30 record, and was $830.00 (+1.8%) early Monday. A new executive order on wind-turbine imports (talks with trading partners, no tariffs yet) could favour it over foreign turbine makers. BofA's Q3 preview (orders about +44% y/y) stands.
risks: Q2 EPS missed ($2.47 vs $3.17) and wind still loses money, so another margin miss on Oct 28 would test the multiple; the stock is below its 50- and 200-day averages.
catalyst: Q3 results Wed Oct 28, webcast 7:30am ET (22:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28).

name: Vertiv
thesis: Vertiv sells power, thermal and liquid-cooling gear for data centres; it guided Q3 sales to $3.65-3.85B and lifted FY26 EPS to $6.65-6.75. It closed Oct 23 at $194.32 and was $196.96 (+1.4%) early Monday after completing the purchase of King Environmental Services, adding fluid-management services in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
risks: The stock trades on the 2027 hyperscaler-capex debate rather than guidance, and price competition in liquid cooling is rising.
catalyst: Q3 results Wed Oct 28 before US open; call 11:00am ET (02:00 AEDT Thu Oct 29).

name: Robinhood
thesis: Robinhood is a retail brokerage adding prediction markets, perpetual futures and Robinhood Agents; Q2 revenue was $1.31B (+32%). Preliminary September data to Sep 24 showed about $267B equity volume, 234M options contracts and 4.4B event contracts. It was $93.55 (-1.6%) early Monday, the day before Q3.
risks: Revenue tracks crypto and equity volumes, and September crypto notional of about $17B (to Sep 24) is soft, so Q3 depends on options and event contracts.
catalyst: Q3 results and full September operating data Tue Oct 27 after close, video call 5pm ET (08:00 AEDT Wed Oct 28).

name: MercadoLibre
thesis: MercadoLibre runs Latin America's largest marketplace, logistics network and Mercado Pago; Q2 net revenue was $10.2B (+50% y/y) while operating income fell 17%. Brazil's electoral court declared Lula the runoff winner with about 51.8% to 48.2%; Flavio Bolsonaro refused to concede and will seek annulment. MELI opened Oct 26 at $1,578 and was $1,598.49 early, down 11.7% from $1,810.15, unwinding the election rally.
risks: Real futures fell about 10% overnight, which cuts reported US-dollar revenue from Brazil, its biggest market; an annulment fight would extend the uncertainty. Margins are being absorbed by the credit book and logistics.
catalyst: Q3 results Nov 4 after US close (provisional, not yet announced by the company; recent calls 5:00pm ET = 09:00 AEDT Thu Nov 5).

name: Cloudflare
thesis: Cloudflare runs a global edge network selling security, CDN, zero-trust and the Workers developer platform; Q2 revenue was $696M (+36%) and it guided Q3 to $736-737M. It closed Oct 23 at $325.73 (+7.3% that day on target raises), up 6.0% since Oct 21 while chips fell.
risks: The stock has had 38 moves of more than 5% in a year and now sits close to the consensus target, so Q3 has to beat and raise.
catalyst: Q3 results Thu Nov 5 after US close, call 5:00pm ET (09:00 AEDT Fri Nov 6).

name: Sea Limited
thesis: Sea runs Shopee, Monee (digital finance) and Garena across Southeast Asia and Brazil; Q2 revenue was $7.79B (+48%). New Street cut it to Neutral from Buy with a $70 target on Oct 26, and it fell 3.5% early to $71.99, a new 52-week low and about 24% below the Oct 16 level, after the Oct 20 memo on launching Sea Cloud.
risks: A new cloud business adds spending with no disclosed budget while Shopee fights TikTok Shop, Temu and Shein; Brazil (a Shopee growth market) took a hit to its currency after Lula's win. DBS and New Street have both cut. Weakest name on the list.
catalyst: Q3 results ~Nov 10 (TBC); any detail on Sea Cloud capex or Monee IPO timing.

name: Keyence
thesis: Keyence sells machine-vision, sensors and measurement gear direct to factories with industry-leading margins and no debt. It closed Oct 26 at JPY 77,270 (about US$492 at 157.0), down 1.4% on the day and 4.5% since Oct 21, a smaller fall than US chip names. Lam's record quarter and supply-constrained guide point to continued fab spending, a core end market.
risks: Orders follow the factory-capex cycle within a quarter, Q1 EPS slightly missed, and a stronger yen (BOJ meets Oct 29-30) cuts reported overseas revenue.
catalyst: Fiscal Q2 results Thu Oct 29 after Tokyo close (time TBC); BOJ decision Fri Oct 30.

name: ASML Holding
thesis: ASML is the only supplier of EUV lithography tools; Q3 sales were a record EUR 11.66B and it guided 2026 to EUR 44-45B, saying 2027-28 supply will not fully meet demand. The ADR fell 6.9% on Oct 22 when Lam warned of supply limits into 2027, closed Oct 23 at $1,571.80, and was $1,601.25 (+1.9%) early Monday. Demand is not the issue.
risks: Semicap is priced for perfection and the SOX is in a bear market (26% off its June high); China is about 20% of ASML sales and export rules can change.
catalyst: Interim dividend EUR 1.88 payable Nov 4; Q4 results January (date TBC).

name: Teradyne
thesis: Teradyne makes test equipment for AI accelerators, HBM and mobile chips, plus Universal Robots; Q3 guidance is $1.20-1.30B revenue and $1.85-2.15 EPS (consensus about $1.26B and $2.05-2.08). It fell 10.6% on Oct 22 and closed Oct 23 at $308.85, down 10.6% since Oct 21. Options price a move of about 13% on the report.
risks: HBM test is a large part of the story, so a weak SK hynix or Samsung print the same week would hit it; test spend is lumpy and concentrated in a few customers.
catalyst: Q3 results Tue Oct 27 after US close (about 07:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28); call Wed Oct 28, 8:30am ET (23:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28).
